subject: Clarify output ownership boundary & feedback license for Order Form (Evergreen Health)
content:
From: Clara Zhao <clara.zhao@evergreenhealth.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, legal@evergreenhealth.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Dec 2025 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on output ownership carveouts + feedback license in Order Form

Hi Lauren (and team),

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our legal team reviewed the latest Order Form and has two areas they want clarified before we proceed to countersign:

1) Output ownership carveouts — Section 4.2 says customer retains rights to "Customer Content" outputs, but the redline language in the Order Form adds a broad training exception for "improving models." Can you confirm whether customer-generated model outputs used for productization (e.g., to fine-tune internal models) would be excluded or not? Our procurement counsel is pushing for a narrow exception limited to telemetry/quality improvements, not model retraining.

2) Feedback license scope — the current MSA grants a perpetual, royalty-free license to use feedback for any purpose. Evergreen wants that narrowed to product-quality signals and anonymized telemetry — no training or derivative model creation.

We attached the redlined doc (see attachment) and highlighted the clauses. Can we get Redwood's legal take and a short, customer-facing summary that we can share internally? We are on a compressed timeline; getting this resolved by Friday 12/12 would help our procurement and security signoffs.

Attachments: Evergreen_MSA_redline_20251208.docx (docx), OrderForm_Evergreen_v3.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Clara
Head of Partnerships
Evergreen Health

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Clara Zhao <clara.zhao@evergreenhealth.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Dec 2025 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on output ownership carveouts + feedback license in Order Form

Clara — thanks for the clear ask and the redline. High-level response: we"re sympathetic to Evergreen's position and happy to propose narrower language that limits training to aggregate/anonymous telemetry and model quality improvement, with an explicit carveout if you opt out of training for production outputs.

Suggested next steps:
- I will loop in Ben (sales) and Monica (solutions) to confirm operational impacts of an opt-out path.
- Rishi (legal) will provide specific redline language for the MSA + Order Form that we can share with your counsel.
- If helpful, we can produce a 1-page summary that your procurement can distribute.

Can we set a 30-min call tomorrow 12/10 at 11am PT to align on the exact carveouts?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Clara Zhao <clara.zhao@evergreenhealth.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Dec 2025 10:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on output ownership carveouts + feedback license in Order Form

Looping in a quick ops perspective: if we add an explicit customer opt-out for "use of customer outputs for model retraining/productization," we need to confirm how that affects caching, KV persistence, and any enterprise telemetry. Practically, opt-out customers will need a flag on their account that disables adding outputs to training pools; we can implement that at provisioning for Dedicated/Private and as an account-level toggle for Hosted.

Monica, can you draft the short operational note for Clara's team outlining what the opt-out means (latency/cost/feature trade-offs)? I can attend the call tomorrow and help with procurement questions.

- Ben

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Clara Zhao <clara.zhao@evergreenhealth.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on output ownership carveouts + feedback license in Order Form

Clara — attaching a short operations note below; copying into the thread so Evergreen has a single document to circulate.

[Attachment stub: Evergreen_MSA_redline_20251208.docx (redlines), OrderForm_Evergreen_v3.pdf]

Operations note (summary):
- Opt-out behavior: When a customer elects to opt-out of output retraining, Redwood will not surface customer outputs into model training pools, nor will outputs be included in datasets used to fine-tune public/shared models.
- Telemetry & quality: We will still collect anonymized telemetry (latency, error rates, token distributions) necessary for platform health and model quality abstractions. These metrics are not derivable back to customer content.
- Feature trade-offs: Customers who opt-out may not receive experimental model improvements derived from cross-customer training. They retain full read/write access to their generated outputs and can export logs on request.
- Implementation timeline: account flag + console UI for opt-out can be enabled within 2 sprints for Hosted customers; Dedicated/Private require a provisioning request.

Please confirm if this aligns with Evergreen's expectations and whether they want the opt-out to be in the MSA or as an Order Form toggled option.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Clara Zhao <clara.zhao@evergreenhealth.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2025 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on output ownership carveouts + feedback license in Order Form

Clara / Evergreen legal — thanks for raising these points. I took a pass at precise redline language below intended for insertion into Section 4 (Customer Content / Outputs) of the MSA and corresponding Order Form clause: please consider these proposals as a starting point — we can iterate based on your counsel's feedback.

Proposed MSA redline (plain language summary first): Redwood will not use Customer Outputs for model training or model-productization activities for accounts that have explicitly elected the "Output Training Opt-Out" in their Order Form. Redwood may continue to use anonymized, aggregated telemetry and non-content-derived signals for platform quality improvements.

Legal redline (for insertion):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Customer may elect in the applicable Order Form an "Output Training Opt-Out" such that (i) Customer Outputs (defined as content generated by Redwood models in response to Customer requests) will not be used by Redwood or its affiliates for the purposes of training, fine-tuning, or otherwise improving models used in production for other customers, and (ii) Redwood may continue to collect anonymized, non-identifying telemetry and feedback for platform operation and quality monitoring. The parties agree that the Opt-Out will take effect upon execution of the Order Form and will apply only to Outputs generated after the effective date.

For avoidance of doubt, Customer grants Redwood a limited, revocable, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use Feedback (non-content commentary, usage signals, and error reports) solely to improve Redwood's platform operations and the performance of models in ways that do not entail incorporating Customer Outputs into underlying model weights or training corpora; such Feedback shall not be used to derive new generative model products that would be commercialized to third parties.

Redwood shall provide reasonable administrative and technical measures to implement and honor the Opt-Out, and shall document the implementation approach in the Service Description."

If Evergreen legal is comfortable with the above, my team can prepare an MSA redline file and a short, plain-language summary for procurement. If not, please indicate the specific language your counsel needs tightened (e.g., duration of opt-out, scope as to derivatives, or data retention carveouts).

Best regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

---

From: Clara Zhao <clara.zhao@evergreenhealth.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, legal@evergreenhealth.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2025 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on output ownership carveouts + feedback license in Order Form

Team — the proposed redline from Rishi looks promising and much closer to what our counsel asked for. Two quick asks before we move to countersign:

1) Can Redwood add a clause specifying that the Opt-Out is reversible only by mutual written agreement (Evergreen wants to prevent accidental unilateral re-enablement).
2) Evergreen legal requests that the phrase "anonymized, non-identifying telemetry" be expanded to list a few concrete examples (latency metrics, tokenization statistics, error rates) to avoid interpretation disputes.

If you can fold those two items into the redline and send the updated doc and the 1-page summary, we can push this through procurement by end of next week. Appreciated.

-Clara

[End of thread]
